ov: Along with the chimpanzee, our closest living relative. Bonobos live only south of the Congo River, in societies where females hold unusual power, and they often settle conflicts through affectionate and sexual contact. They mainly eat fruit.
len: 70–83 cm (nose to rump, on all fours)
rg: A 500,000 km² area of the Congo Basin in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, south of the Congo River.

cf.tip: Bonobos live south of the Congo River and chimpanzees north of it; chimps hunt far more, eating monkeys and small antelope.

fx: Neither bonobos nor chimps swim well, so the Congo River may have split their ancestors into two species.
Bonobos typically live 40 years in captivity; their wild lifespan is unknown.
